newsitem.title: USA: Epson gets injunction vs Nu-Kote, Pelikan.
newsitem.headline: Epson gets injunction vs Nu-Kote, Pelikan.

text.p: Epson America Inc said Thursday a federal court ordered an injunction against the sale of various ink jet printer cartridges made by Nu-Kote Holdings Inc's Nu-Kote International and Pelikan Holding AG's Pelikan Productions.

Epson, an affiliate of Japan's Seiko Corp, said the U.S. District Court in Los Angeles ordered Nu-Kote to stop making and selling its RF60, RF61 and RF62 cartridges and ordered Pelikan to stop making and selling its Z630, Z653 and Z654 cartridges.

Epson said the court extended its 1995 preliminary injunction to include any infringement of Epson's '401 patent, which is a braodly-based patent dealing with the way cartridges supply ink to printers.
The company added the court also awarded Epson more than $1 million on August 11 for Nu-Kote's selling ink cartridges in violation of the earlier injunction.

Lastly, the court denied Nu-Kote motion for summary judgement on Epson's '401 patent but granted Nu-Kote summary judgement on one of Epson's design patents," the company said, adding it will appeal the ruling on the design patent.
Nu-Kote, which is embroiled in similar disputes with Canon Inc and Hewlett-Packard Co, has filed a counter claim, alleging anti-trust violations by Epson.

Canon won a preliminary injunction against Nu-Kote in federal court on March 18, which blocked Nu-Kote from making and selling replacement ink cartridges for Canon's BJC-6000 series Bubble Jet Printers.

Nu-Kote had its day in court when a federal judge in San Jose, Calif., ruled in July 11 Hewlett-Packard falsely labeled packages for its inkjet cartridges to make consumers believe cartridges made by other companies are incompatible with its printers.
The court July 24 accepted Hewlett-Packard's proposal to change its product illustration on packages of two of its black inkjet cartridges but rebuffed all remedies sought by Nu-Kote.
Nu-Kote said Thursday in as statement it had redesigned its Epson-compatible inkjet cartridges "to avoid any issues in the lawsuit brought by Seiko-Epson."
The company said Thursday's injunction against its RF60, RF61 and RF62 cartridges "applies to an older model product which has been discontinued."
The company added it is currently shipping its redesigned inkjet cartridges and that the court ruling has no impact on its current product line.
Nu-Kote and Epson spokesmen could not not immediately comment on the status of Nu-Kote's redesigned cartridges.
Nu-Kote's stock fell 1/8 to 1-15/16 Thursday morning.
